scenarios.title: Annual compounding at 10% for 10,000 years
scenarios.why: Ten thousand years of annual compounding grows $10,000 to about 10^418, past every fixed-point word: at 10% 64.64 overflows by N = 365, Solady, Balancer, Maker and FP127 by N = 1,000 and PRBMath by N = 10,000 (at 50%, 64.64 by N = 100 and the rest by N = 365); only binary128 and FP256 reach N = 10,000. Until about N = 20 the balances are short decimals that WAD and RAY hold exactly. The row began as a check of an old README claim ($25,937.42 true against $25,932.38 for Solady at N = 10); Solady returns $25,937.424601 exactly.

scenarios.title: Continuous accrual
scenarios.result: balance after N days of continuous accrual
scenarios.why: How Aave and Morpho accrue: the ideal is e^(rate * time), and both ship a three-term expansion of it (1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6), which Aave notes 'slightly underpays liquidity providers and undercharges borrowers'. Every library is judged against the exponential it approximates. The step here is one accrual spanning N days, which is what a market that nobody touched for N days computes on its next interaction; the expansion's error is x^4/24 with x = rate * years, so it is invisible at daily updates and the whole story at a year or more. Morpho holds the rate per second in WAD (1,585,489,599 wei at 5% APR), ten significant digits before any arithmetic; both digit counts show that loss, since the format truth is built from the annual rate the other libraries receive.

scenarios.title: An option walking out of the money
scenarios.step: S = S (1 - tick); then C = S N(d1) - K e^(-rT) N(d2)
scenarios.result: the Black-Scholes call price after N down-ticks of the spot
scenarios.why: Options protocols price with N(d), the normal distribution function, and the spot walks. Near the money every library agrees; past d = -8 an 18-decimal N(d) is zero and the price with it, and before that e^(-d^2/2) has lost most of its digits. FP127 and FP256 have normCdf as an op; the other libraries run the same series and continued fraction through their own exp, sqrt, mul and div, with pi by Ramanujan through the same ops, so each is judged on its primitives. Relative digits there say little about money: at N = 10,000 the true price of five of the six inputs is below 10^-15 wei of a $100 strike at 18 decimals, so every library is off by less than a wei; the slow walk's is 3.2 million wei ($3 × 10^-12), where the WAD libraries are off by about 94 wei. Up to N = 1,000 they are off by tens to ten thousand wei, FP127 by under 10^-16 (absErrWei in the data).

scenarios.title: Decay, the share released
scenarios.result: the share released after N steps of decay
scenarios.why: Vesting, TWAP weights and exponential moving averages multiply by e^(-dt/tau) every step. The factor is a hair below one, and on an 18-decimal grid eps and e^(-eps) both sit on a grid of spacing 1e-18, so the factor's distance from one keeps about 18 + log10(eps) digits, and the released share with it: six digits at eps = 1.06e-12, three at 1.06e-15, one at 1.06e-17, and below 1e-18 nothing is released at all. Each eps is dt/tau for a time constant in seconds, which no grid holds exactly; a power of ten sits on the WAD grid and flatters it (at eps = 1e-17 exactly, Solady kept 17 digits).
